title: O DISCLOSE Thy Lovely Face
description: O DISCLOSE Thy Lovely Face in Tonic Solfa to SPANISH HYMN, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 156. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to SPANISH HYMN; any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: O DIS-CLOSE thy love-ly face! Quick-en all my droop-ing powers; Gasps my faint-ing soul for grace, As a thirst-y land for showers; Haste, my Lord, no more de-lay, Come, my Sa-viour, come a-way!

lines: Gasps my fainting soul for grace,
As a thirsty land for showers;
Haste, my Lord, no more delay,
Well thou know'st I cannot rest
Till I fully rest in thee,
Till I am of thee possessed,
Till from every sin set free,
All the life of faith I prove,
All the joy and heaven of love.
Keep me, or from thee I fly;
Strength and comfort from thy word
Make me faithful to the end.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SPANISH HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
